title: Outlook: grant mailbox and folder delegate permissions from the new Outlook
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents policies restricting folder-permission changes in new Outlook, so the statement that no admin control is documented is misleading. The folder-permission UI is also documented, and the checklist incorrectly suggests using permission-granting commands to list existing delegates.

claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook grant delegate mailbox folder sharing permissions 417063 default policy; "new Outlook" "delegate" "sharing" "permissions". Read recipient permissions, Add-MailboxFolderPermission and calendar delegate permissions; no mapping to the planned screens found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk

claims.claim: No administrator control restricting users' delegate-sharing actions in new Outlook is documented.
claims.quote: Restrict users from changing folder permissions in classic Outlook, new Outlook, and Outlook on the Web
claims.fix: Replace the no-control statements with: 'Learn documents Cloud Policy restrictions on folder-permission changes in new Outlook, using Turn off sharing recommendation, Do not allow users to change permissions on folders, and Control Calendar Sharing. A switch specifically for all of this roadmap item's new screens is not documented.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/outlook/configuration/restrict-users-from-modifying-folder-permissions. Narrow the open question to whether a separate switch covers the complete new capability; do not imply that existing folder-permission restrictions are absent.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users assigned Full Access, Send as or Send on behalf on another mailbox are called delegates.
claims.quote: The users that are assigned these permissions on other mailboxes or groups are called delegates.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Full Access allows a delegate to open the mailbox and view, add and remove its contents.
claims.quote: Allows the delegate to open the mailbox, and view, add and remove the contents of the mailbox.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Send as makes a message appear to come directly from the mailbox without indicating the delegate sent it.
claims.quote: Allows the delegate to send messages as if they came directly from the mailbox or group. There's no indication that the message was sent by the delegate.

claims.claim: Send on behalf identifies the delegate in the From address.
claims.quote: The From address of these messages clearly shows that the message was sent by the delegate

claims.claim: An Outlook calendar delegate has the Editor calendar role.
claims.quote: An Outlook delegate has the Editor calendar role and a Delegate sharing permission flag.

claims.claim: An Outlook calendar delegate has the Delegate sharing permission flag.
claims.quote: An Outlook delegate has the Editor calendar role and a Delegate sharing permission flag.

claims.claim: Learn recommends configuring delegate relationships from Outlook while the calendar owner is signed in.
claims.quote: Configure delegate relationships from Outlook while the calendar owner is signed in.

claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell is appropriate for calendar folder permission administration.
claims.quote: Exchange Online PowerShell is appropriate for calendar folder permission administration and validation

claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell is not the preferred method for creating a complete delegate relationship.
claims.quote: it isn't the preferred method for creating a complete delegate relationship.

claims.claim: Calendar delegate access does not include viewing private items by default; CanViewPrivateItems is a separate flag.
claims.quote: CanViewPrivateItems lets the user view private calendar items. Delegate access doesn't include this capability by default.

claims.claim: Exchange admin center > Recipients > Mailboxes > mailbox > Mailbox delegation reaches the mailbox delegate-permissions page.
claims.quote: In the EAC, click Recipients in the feature pane. ... Mailboxes: User or linked mailboxes. ... select the mailbox ... Click Mailbox Delegation
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct page but stops before the assignment control. For Full Access, extend it to 'Recipients > Mailboxes > mailbox > Mailbox Delegation > Read and manage (Full Access) > Edit > Add members', using the same cited page.

claims.claim: Add-MailboxPermission -Identity <MailboxIdentity> -User <DelegateIdentity> -AccessRights FullAccess -InheritanceType All grants mailbox Full Access.
claims.quote: Add-MailboxPermission -Identity <MailboxIdentity> -User <DelegateIdentity> -AccessRights FullAccess -InheritanceType All [-AutoMapping $false]

claims.claim: Add-RecipientPermission manages Send as permissions.
claims.quote: You use the Add-RecipientPermission and Remove-RecipientPermission cmdlets to manage the Send As permission for mailboxes and groups.

claims.claim: Set-Mailbox with GrantSendOnBehalfTo manages Send on behalf permissions on mailboxes.
claims.quote: Set-Mailbox -Identity seanc@contoso.com -GrantSendOnBehalfTo hollyh

claims.claim: No UI is documented for setting which users hold permissions on a mailbox folder.
claims.quote: Right-click the folder that you want to move, and then select Properties. ... On the Permissions tab ... Select Add. ... Select your name, and then select Owner for the Permission Level.
claims.fix: Replace the null side with the documented existing Outlook UI: surface 'Outlook (classic)', path 'mailbox folder (right-click) > Properties > Permissions > Add > user > Add > OK > user > Permission Level', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/outlook/user-interface/cannot-copy-this-folder-because-it-may-contain-private-items'. Qualify it as the existing Outlook folder-permission UI, not an Exchange admin center route or documentation of the planned new screens.

claims.claim: Add-MailboxFolderPermission -Identity <mailbox>:\<folder> -User <user> -AccessRights <role> grants folder permissions.
claims.quote: Add-MailboxFolderPermission -Identity ayla@contoso.com:\Marketing -User ed@contoso.com -AccessRights Owner

claims.claim: SharingPermissionFlags Delegate is documented for calendar folders.
claims.quote: This parameter only applies to calendar folders and can only be used when the AccessRights parameter value is Editor.

claims.quote: By default, for a user mailbox, Information Rights Management (IRM)-protected email messages can be read by any delegate who has Full Access permission on the mailbox.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout

claims.claim: Sharing a mailbox subfolder requires permissions on the folder and its parent folders.
claims.quote: the user has to grant the other person access to the specific folder that the user wants to share and also to all other parent folders in the folder hierarchy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The root Mailbox folder must have at least Folder visible permissions for the default role.

claims.claim: Insufficient access to another user's mailbox folder can produce the stated Unable to open default folders error.
claims.quote:
Unable to open default folders-you do not have permissions to logon

This issue occurs if the user doesn't have sufficient permissions to access the mailbox folder.

claims.claim: The existing Exchange procedures require assigned permissions and refer readers to the Mailbox settings entry for the requirements.
claims.quote: You need to be assigned permissions before you can perform this procedure or procedures. To see what permissions you need, see the "Mailbox settings" entry in the Feature permissions in Exchange Online article.

claims.claim: Documentation checked does not settle whether both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows get the planned new screens.
claims.quote: Searched: "417063" "shared" "resource" "web" "Windows"; "new Outlook" "delegate" "sharing" "permissions". Read the record and add-in setup excerpts for Web and new Outlook; no statement settling both clients' coverage by the planned screens found.

claims.claim: The existing Exchange permission-management options differ by mailbox type.
claims.quote: Send on behalf: Messages sent by a delegate have "<Delegate> on behalf of <Mailbox>" in the From address. Note that this permission isn't available in the EAC for shared mailboxes.
